key_insight: CA-WCP makes 3D segmentation uncertainty more reliable by using class-specific asymmetric bounds and shift-aware weighting instead of a single symmetric interval.
clinical_relevance: This could improve how volumetric tumor or organ segmentation uncertainty is communicated in radiology workflows, especially when models face distribution shift.
method: Uses latent-space density-ratio weighting to handle covariate shift.
Builds directional lower and upper volume bounds with conformal prediction.
Adjusts each class by false-positive/false-negative asymmetry factors from validation data.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on BraTS 2020 brain tumor segmentation and a synthetic multi-organ CT shift benchmark; the abstract reports 95% Clopper-Pearson coverage intervals containing the nominal 90% level for every class and 8-14% narrower intervals than symmetric weighted conformal prediction.
watch_item: The approach depends on representative validation data and carefully estimated shift weights, so performance may degrade if these inputs are inaccurate or if deployment shifts beyond the calibration setting.
paper_title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
